rulings.challenge_claim: That the sentence disclosing the opening verse's mark is grammatically broken and should be repaired for clarity, the underlying mark facts being sound; and that the same sentence contradicts itself about what the mark does, that a byte-true negated-obedience clause brackets oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7 across the row's own closing seam undisclosed, and that a device note claims both name spellings are given as the bytes carry them while only one is spliced.
rulings.grounds: The two items land on one row and are partly one defect. SENTENCE (same defect site, both items): the boundary rationale reads that oshb:Jer.43.1 'is marked with a closing setumah (...) falls inside this same opening verse', two finite predicates on one subject, and the sentence after it opens lowercase on 'disclosed here as texture:'. The prose break is real, but the clarity-only reading understates it: the parashah layer is keyed by verse (303 marked verses, type recorded per verse, single-witness, tier-3) and carries no intra-verse positions, so 'falls inside this same opening verse' is not sourceable from it; what the inventory records at that key is a setumah closing oshb:Jer.43.1, correctly typed and never conflated with petuchah. The mis-stated shape stands a second time in strongest_rejected_alternative ('the setumah that falls inside it'), so it sits on load-bearing prose, not decoration. Upheld at medium, not low. CROSS-SEAM CONSTRUCTION (refined): the negated obey-the-voice construction does stand either side of the row's own closing seam, וְלֹֽא שָׁמַע֩ ... בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.43.4, byte) and כִּ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.43.7, byte), and no field of the row names it, so a disclosure is owed under the cross-seam-cohesion rule; the construction stands in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, 11 token occurrences), 6 of them inside oshb:Jer.42.6-oshb:Jer.44.23. Three corrections to the framing: it is verse-medial at both sites, closing the etnachta colon while oshb:Jer.43.4 runs on to the dwelling-in-Judah phrase and oshb:Jer.43.7 to the arrival at Tahpanhes, so neither verse ends with it; the two are not one clause repeated, the verb being singular of Johanan at the first site and plural of the whole company at the second; and it does not bracket oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7, since oshb:Jer.43.1 carries no instance -- the two instances close two consecutive units, which corroborates a cut between them as readily as it argues continuity across it. Disclosure gap real; the continuity reading is not carried by these bytes. NAME FORM (upheld): device_notes states both spellings are given exactly as the bytes carry them, but only עֲזַרְיָ֤ה בֶן הוֹשַֽׁעְיָה֙ (oshb:Jer.43.2, byte) is spliced; no Hebrew form from oshb:Jer.42.1, וִֽיזַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן הוֹשַֽׁעְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.42.1, byte), appears in any of the row's 22 fields. The two patronymics are consonantally identical and their pointing differs only in the accent, so the claim is true but unquoted on one side. The span itself is not contested.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: rewrite the opening-verse disclosure as two complete sentences -- one stating that the inventory records a setumah closing oshb:Jer.43.1 (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration not driver), one stating the setumah closing oshb:Jer.42.22 -- and delete the 'falls inside this same opening verse' position claim; restore sentence-initial capitalisation at the second. strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the rival on the mark as the inventory records it (a segment close at oshb:Jer.43.1), keeping the existing answer that the opening verse is the temporal clause governing the accusation after it; the sentence stays one sentence. boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose the negated obey-the-voice construction recurring at oshb:Jer.43.4 and oshb:Jer.43.7 with a digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit (sweep: 10 verses), stating it is verse-medial at both and that the seam is not overturned by it. device_notes: either splice the oshb:Jer.42.1 patronymic beside the oshb:Jer.43.2 form, each with its own oshb: ref and tier named, or narrow the claim to the one form actually quoted. TESTS the cure must pass: no mark claim may assert an intra-verse position for a verse-keyed layer, and every mark claim must validate under its claimed type at its MT key; the cross-seam device must carry a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; every form claimed as given as the bytes carry it must stand in the row as a byte-tier splice with its own ref; the replacement rejected alternative must still name a real rival. No boundary change is proposed or implied by any of this.

rulings.challenge_claim: That the row twice describes the following word-event as a dated notice, which its bytes do not carry, and that it sits at high confidence on an onset carrying no formula, vocative, or participant change, with the negated-obedience clause bracketing oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7 across that onset likewise undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Both charges stand as made. DATE LABEL: oshb:Jer.43.8 reads וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בְּתַחְפַּנְחֵ֖ס לֵאמֹֽר (byte) -- a verse-initial narrative word-event formula with a place adjunct and the quotative, carrying no year, month, regnal or ordinal element; the second witness carries none either, “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,” (web:Jer.43.8). The verse is absent from the 19 classified date-header candidate sites and present among the 21 verses carrying that formula (sweep: 21 verses; the single non-initial site is oshb:Jer.42.7), so the tier-1 driver named for the close is byte-true and only the dated qualifier fails. It fails twice: once in the closing warrant and once in strongest_rejected_alternative, where it is the stated ground for not carrying past the seam. CALIBRATION: the onset reads וַיִּקַּ֞ח יוֹחָנָ֤ן בֶּן קָרֵ֨חַ֙ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.43.5, byte) -- the same actors already named at oshb:Jer.43.4, a narrative action verb, and no formula, vocative, addressee change or participant change; only the close is formula-bound. The row nonetheless sits at high with frontier_flag_considered false, while the adjoining span at Jer.43.1-Jer.43.4, whose edges are of the same softness, sits a step lower. I do not contest the span: the turn from the verbal refusal to the taking-and-going is a defensible scene seam. What fails is the posture, and confidence is an ordinary row field, so correcting it is not a respan. BRACKET SUB-ITEM: real but re-framed. The negated obey-the-voice construction at oshb:Jer.43.4 and oshb:Jer.43.7 is undisclosed here as well and is owed a disclosure, but it is verse-medial at both sites rather than verse-final, the verb differs in number between them, and it saturates this arc -- 6 of its 10 book-wide verses (sweep: 10 verses, 11 token occurrences) fall inside oshb:Jer.42.6-oshb:Jer.44.23 -- so it is complex-wide texture owed disclosure, not a seam-specific counter-device.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the dated qualifier at both occurrences and state the close on what the bytes carry -- a verse-initial word-event formula with a place adjunct at Tahpanhes, one of 21 verses carrying that formula (sweep: 21 verses); the rejected alternative stays one sentence and must still reject the rival on the formula alone. confidence: lower from high to medium, and set frontier_flag_considered true, on the ground that the front seam carries no tier-1 device of its own while the close does; this is a field edit only, the span is unchanged. device_notes or boundary_rationale: disclose the negated obey-the-voice construction at oshb:Jer.43.4 and oshb:Jer.43.7 with a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit (sweep: 10 verses), noting it is verse-medial at both and stands across this arc rather than at this seam alone. TESTS the cure must pass: no date-class label may stand on a verse that is absent from the classified date-header object and carries no year, month, regnal or ordinal element in its own bytes; a high confidence must not stand where the front seam carries no tier-1 device; the cross-seam device must be named with a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit.

rulings.challenge_claim: That two paseq entries inside the span go undisclosed while the four setumah in the same verses are itemized in detail; and that the span treats its second internal messenger formula as a restatement of the same full divine title when that formula's bytes carry a different and far rarer stack, the blend sitting under the rejected alternative that declines a cut there.
rulings.grounds: One shared defect and one distinct defect, both upheld. PASEQ (same defect, both items): the inventory carries one paseq seg at oshb:Jer.44.9 and one at oshb:Jer.44.14 (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position sourceable), and no field of the row names the paseq layer at all, while device_notes itemizes the setumah closing oshb:Jer.44.1, oshb:Jer.44.6, oshb:Jer.44.10 and oshb:Jer.44.14 and presents that itemization as the stretch's texture disclosed in full. Span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry is unconditional and layer-blind, so an itemized parashah disclosure beside a silent paseq layer in the same verses is an incomplete disclosure, not a settled posture. The ordinals offered -- the span's ninth verse and its closing fourteenth -- map correctly onto oshb:Jer.44.9 and oshb:Jer.44.14 for a span opening at oshb:Jer.44.1, so the object behind the digits is right and not merely the digits. The boundary argument is untouched: paseq is count-only and never a driver. TITLE STACK (distinct defect): oshb:Jer.44.2 carries כֹּה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (byte) and oshb:Jer.44.11 carries כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (byte), both members of the full-stack object attested in 32 verses (sweep: 32 verses). oshb:Jer.44.7 carries כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (byte) -- an elohei-augmented stack standing in exactly 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses: oshb:Jer.35.17, oshb:Jer.38.17, oshb:Jer.44.7) and not a member of the 32-verse object, the full-stack run not being a substring of it. Calling the ve'atah movement a restatement of the full divine title blends two byte-distinct count objects, and it does so where the blend bears weight: strongest_rejected_alternative declines a cut at that position on the ground that both internal restatements are recurrences of one formula, so the one stack in this span outside that object is exactly what the rival had to weigh and did not. Two fairness notes that do not move the verdict: the row's splice of oshb:Jer.44.7 is itself byte-correct, so the defect is the class label and the rival's engagement rather than the quotation; and the 153-verse census cited for the density argument is correctly applied to its own object, all three sites being koh-amar onsets in the same divine mouth. The header seam is not contested -- oshb:Jer.44.1 carries the aleph-lamed superscription shape, one of 11 sites (sweep: 11 verses). NEW FINDING neither item names: boundary_rationale opens mid-sentence on a lowercase word, 'a setumah closes oshb:Jer.43.13 ...', the same drafting artifact carried by the row at Jer.43.1-Jer.43.4.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the paseq disclosure for oshb:Jer.44.9 and oshb:Jer.44.14 beside the existing setumah itemization -- single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted -- and drop or qualify the disclosed-in-full framing so it matches what is actually disclosed. boundary_rationale: replace 'restating the full divine title' at the ve'atah movement with the form the row actually splices, named as its own count object with its digit (sweep: 3 verses), and keep the full-stack object with its own digit (sweep: 32 verses) for oshb:Jer.44.2 and oshb:Jer.44.11; also capitalise the field's opening sentence. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-argue the declined cut at oshb:Jer.44.7 with the distinct stack weighed -- the answer may still stand on the unchanged speaker and addressee, but it must engage the form difference instead of treating both restatements as one formula's recurrence; one sentence, plus the mandated rival-disclosure sentence if used. TESTS the cure must pass: span-relevant mark disclosure must cover every layer with an entry inside the span, not one layer only; no divine-title claim may blend the 32-verse full stack with the 3-verse elohei-augmented stack, and each must name its swept object and digit; the replacement rejected alternative must still name a real rival and survive the form difference that killed the original. No boundary change is proposed: the span stands.
